name: MD-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Open seat after Hoyer's retirement, but Democratic nominee Boafo heavily funded
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: The seat sits in a D+17 district and Hoyer's retirement does not change the underlying partisanship. Boafo has raised over $1.6 million with more than $12 million in outside support and no opposition spending, while markets price the Democratic side near 97%, all consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a closer race or unexpected outside spending against Boafo would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Steny Hoyer (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Steny Hoyer's retirement opens Maryland's 5th District, but the seat remains firmly Democratic territory with a D+17 partisan lean. Democrat Adrian Boafo enters the general election with a strong financial position, having raised about $1.7 million and benefited from roughly $12 million in outside support, with no recorded spending opposing him. Republican Chris Chaffee reports minimal disclosed fundraising.

No general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and money. Prediction markets put the Democratic side near 97%, and the fundamentals point to a Democratic margin in the low twenties. The race is rated Safe D, with uncertainty reflecting the absence of polling rather than any sign of competitiveness.
